clue.text: Locks cleaner in the bathroom?

parts.note: locks are tresses of hair, not door fastenings, so the cleaner is a hair wash kept by the bath

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what a cleaning product for door locks is doing in the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' suggests door hardware; read it as hair and the cleaner is the bottle by the shower.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair is made up of locks, and the liquid that washes hair sits in the bathroom.

clue.text: Peels off outfits

definitions.meaning: to peel off is to remove a covering, take off a layer
football teams' kits are their colours or uniforms

explanation.surface: Someone takes off their clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Peels off as a verb means removes; as a noun, sports teams wear these as uniforms.

clue.text: One entering a party removing top in titillation — it creates a lot of buzz

definitions.text: it creates a lot of buzz

indicators.note: entering says the numeral goes into the shortened phrase
removing says a letter is taken out of the phrase
top in means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone arriving at a racy party causes quite a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top in titillation' is T; 'removing' it from A PARTY gives APARY; 'entering' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A place full of beehives is literally humming, so it makes much buzzing noise.

clue.text: Very softly hugging feverish old gran — almost hard to take a picture

indicators.note: hugging says the two soft letters wrap round the middle pieces

parts.note: PP, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very softly
feverish means hot

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, short for grandmother
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tender hug for a feverish granny before a difficult snapshot.
explanation.walkthrough: PP is the musical marking pianissimo; 'almost' and 'hugging' are the signals, with the pencil-grade H at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To photograph something is to capture its image with a camera.

clue.text: Greek character's great with nothing on

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the letter for nothing above the other piece

parts.note: O is the shape of zero, nothing
mega is slang for great

explanation.surface: A Greek man is described as wonderful while wearing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person; it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the last letter of the alphabet used in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Criticised a couple of males in sleigh

indicators.note: in says the article and the pair of male letters sit inside the sledge word

parts.note: a sleigh is a sled
M is the abbreviation for male, so two of them make MM

explanation.surface: Two men riding in a sleigh come in for criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: To slam a play or a policy is to criticise it harshly, a common informal synonym.

clue.text: A report is in place for space station, perhaps

indicators.note: is in says these letters sit inside the location word

parts.note: a site is a place
to tell is to report or recount

explanation.surface: A news item says a location has been picked for an orbital base.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbiting space station is one example of a man-made body circling Earth.

clue.text: Relative to jeer at? Not at first

indicators.note: not at first says the opening letter is left off

parts.note: to jeer at someone is to taunt them

explanation.surface: A family member one is tempted to mock, but holds back initially.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's sister is a family member, a close relation.

clue.text: Chief with volunteers in support

parts.note: chief means main, principal
the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A leader joins the volunteers in backing a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's part-time volunteer army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a family is to provide for it, keep it going financially.

clue.text: Fantasising in day about a Chinese dynasty

parts.note: re means about, concerning
the Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644

explanation.surface: Someone lost in daydreams about China's imperial past.
explanation.definitionFit: Indulging in fantasy is letting the mind wander in pleasant imaginings, as in a reverie.

clue.text: Animal — one encapsulated by extraordinary horn

indicators.note: encapsulated by says the letter for one is enclosed within the rearranged letters
extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so the letters of horn are put in an unusual order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An animal with one remarkable horn, a neat nod to the creature itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' rearranges HORN into RHNO, and 'encapsulated by' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large thick-skinned African or Asian beast, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Large, overpriced piano swapped for clarinet, ultimately

indicators.note: swapped for says one letter is taken out and another put in its place

parts.note: overpriced means costing too much, expensive
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the instrument named

explanation.surface: A big, overpriced piano gets traded in for a clarinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapped for' replaces the P in EXPENSIVE with T, the last letter of clarinet ('ultimately').
explanation.definitionFit: Something wide-ranging or covering a big area is extensive, a synonym of large in scale.

clue.text: Individual friend in my book

parts.note: an individual is a person
a friend is an ally

explanation.surface: Someone declares that, in their view, a particular friend is special.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Individual' looks like an adjective in the surface but is the noun meaning a single human being.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'in my book' means in my own opinion, speaking for myself.

clue.text: Stop heads of state trivialising every meeting

indicators.note: heads of takes the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A call to end politicians making light of every summit meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to stop or staunch it, as in stemming the bleeding.

clue.text: Female a distance away is enthralled

indicators.note: away means out of place, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A man is captivated by a woman seen from afar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' looks like part of the distance but rearranges A DISTANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enthralled is to be captivated, held spellbound by something.

clue.text: Running over before Saigon train's off

indicators.note: before says the letter for over comes first, ahead of the rest

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A train leaving Saigon seems to be going on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' looks like a train in motion but means management. 'off' is the anagram signal; the 's of train's is read as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The running of a business means its management, the way it is arranged and directed.

clue.text: Northern big cat died after article's published

indicators.note: after says the remaining pieces follow the article

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A newspaper story reports the death of a big cat in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of article's is read as 'is', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something announced has been made public, declared openly.

clue.text: I'd pulled up small flower — catastrophe!

indicators.note: pulled up, in a down clue, says the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, with the apostrophe dropped
the aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A gardener pulled up a little flower by mistake and calls it a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled up' turns ID into DI.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe is a calamity, a great misfortune.

clue.text: Promotes loans

definitions.meaning: money lent ahead of time, such as against salary

explanation.surface: A bank pushes its lending products.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means helps forward; as a plural noun, sums of money lent beforehand.

clue.text: Ended nice novel, welcoming writer's lack of bias

indicators.note: welcoming says the shuffled letters take in the writing tool
novel means new or fresh, so the letters are made into a new order

parts.note: a pen is a writer's instrument

explanation.surface: An author finishes a pleasant novel, praised for being even-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book being finished but is the anagram signal; 'welcoming' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Independence of mind means freedom from outside influence, hence impartiality.

clue.text: Quiet Yorkshire town

definitions.meaning: to quiet something is to calm it down
a market town in North Yorkshire, on the famous scenic railway line to Carlisle

explanation.surface: A peaceful little town in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle is a small market town in North Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to calm or still; also the name of a small North Yorkshire market town.

clue.text: Mature people from America strangely lust after diamonds

indicators.note: after says the shuffled letters come after the card-suit letter

parts.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of lust are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Grown-ups from the US have a weird craving for diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns LUST into ULTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Grown-ups are fully developed individuals, as opposed to children.

clue.text: The first man advanced and cuckoo retreated

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

indicators.note: retreated says the word goes backwards, read right to left

parts.note: cuckoo means crazy, mad

explanation.surface: The first human advanced boldly, then fled in a crazy panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreated' turns MAD back to DAM.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis he is the first human created by God, the original man.

clue.text: Supported aunt and agreed changes

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An aunt backed the plan and agreed to some amendments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' shuffles AUNT and AGREED together.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan that is guaranteed is backed or underwritten by someone, so supported.

clue.text: Sounds like expensive car parts

indicators.note: sounds like says the word must be said aloud to match the entry

parts.note: a Rolls, short for Rolls-Royce, is a luxury car

explanation.surface: Someone notes the cost of components for a luxury vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like car components but means acting roles.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors play parts, the characters assigned to them in a play.

clue.text: Up-to-date Foreign Office details

parts.note: in means fashionable, current
FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office, the UK ministry of external affairs

explanation.surface: The Foreign Office issues its latest briefing.
explanation.definitionFit: Info is informal short for information, the facts or particulars given.

clue.text: Specialist from Switzerland mostly pleasant in greenish-blue

indicators.note: in says the middle pieces sit inside the colour word

parts.note: teal is a greenish-blue colour
CH is the international code for Switzerland

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: pleasant means nice

explanation.surface: An expert from Switzerland, quite agreeable, dressed in blue-green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims NICE to NIC; CH plus NIC goes 'in' TEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical language belongs to a particular field or trade, so it is specialised.

clue.text: Little child with a large sum

parts.note: a tot is a small child
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A toddler is handed a big amount of money.
explanation.definitionFit: The total is the whole amount when numbers are added together.

clue.text: Reply from Greeks oddly ignored small body of water

indicators.note: oddly ignored drops the first, third and fifth letters, keeping the rest

parts.note: a pond is a small stretch of still water

explanation.surface: A reply arrives from Greeks who pointedly overlooked a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly ignored' leaves RES from Greeks.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond is to answer, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Departments send a subsidy back showing regret

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
showing says the letters are on display inside the words before it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Government departments are sorry to be sending out a grant.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft named no signal for the concealment; 'showing' supplies it, and 'back' reverses the run found across the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Regret is a feeling of sorrow, a near synonym of unhappiness.
